docRequirement: sub-agents.md:904 (§ Concurrent subagent limit) binds the Agent-tool spawn path to a per-session ceiling of 20 RUNNING subagents that FAILS the spawn with the message `Concurrent subagent limit reached` and tells the model not to retry; the ceiling is overridable through `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (any positive whole number) and is not enforced at all in a session with ultracode (max effort) active. :908 exempts an in-session `/subtask` fork — it 'takes a slot while it runs and is never blocked by the limit'; :909 lets a resume take a fresh slot without a check; :911 says agents other features run — workflow agents, agent-team teammates — 'follow their own limits instead', i.e. the subagent ceiling and the workflow ceiling are two limits, not one.
current: One module-level FIFO semaphore gates every child spawn in the Pi subprocess. `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:103) is narrowed at runtime to `Math.max(1, Math.min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2))` (spawner.ts:136-142), and the singleton is built from it at spawner.ts:204 and rebuilt per capability generation at spawner.ts:208. Every spawn body — start, plus the background `monitorWithAbort` wait, so a slot is held for the child's whole life — runs inside `semaphore.run` at spawner.ts:587-649. An over-limit caller is QUEUED, never refused: `Semaphore.acquire` (spawner.ts:165-186) pushes a waiter and rejects only on an aborted signal. All five spawn paths share that one gate: the Agent tool (subagent-tool.ts:282, :316), workflow `agent()` (workflow-tool.ts:358, :390 via the `spawn` resolved at :466), review (review-tool.ts:309), guardian judge (guardian-runner.ts:57) and the `/subtask` fork (subtask.ts:95). The collapse is already written down as ours: packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46 gives `concurrency` default `16`, 'Applies to: `subagent`, `workflow`'. The value 16 and the CPU narrowing are exactly the WORKFLOW contract (workflows.md:320, 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores'), so the subagent half sits 4 below spec and shares a limit the doc says is separate. There is no env reader: `grep -ra` over packages/ apps/ returns zero hits for `MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` and zero source hits for `Concurrent subagent limit`; `concurrency` reaches the subprocess only as `PiOrchestratorConfig.concurrency` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:30, default 16 at :103, validated at :250), which no host code ever sets — SessionManager.ts:4152 builds the manifest seed without it. No ultracode exemption exists in the spawner, although the session's effort is already readable at spawn time (`sessionThinkingLevel(cfg)`, spawner.ts:271-273) and the workflow path already expresses ultracode as `thinkingLevel === 'max'` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1504). `/subtask` is not exempt: it enters the same semaphore via subtask.ts:95 and `startSubtaskFork` awaits admission (subtask.ts:137-142), so a saturated gate stalls the command. Resume is outside the gate entirely (subagent-tool.ts:474 calls `childSessionPort.resume`, and the host's `resume` flips status back to `running` with no concurrency check, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:216-234). The only hard concurrency FAILURE we own is host-side and different: `child-session-service.ts:149` throws `child-session-concurrency-limit` when active children reach `budgets.concurrency` — the un-narrowed 16 the spawner sends at spawner.ts:604 — which the subprocess semaphore (always <= that) makes practically unreachable, and whose message is a host-internal string, not the doc's model-facing one.
divergence: Not a wrong key name — a missing second limit plus a wrong failure mode. Four deltas: (1) SCOPE — one semaphore serves both the Agent-tool path and the workflow path, where the doc specifies two independent ceilings (:911); the workflow number (16, narrowed by `cpuCores - 2`) is correct for workflows and is being applied to subagents. (2) THRESHOLD — the subagent ceiling should be 20 flat; ours is `min(16, cpuCores - 2)`, i.e. 6 on an 8-core machine, 2 on a 4-core one. (3) FAILURE MODE — an over-limit Agent-tool spawn must FAIL with `Concurrent subagent limit reached` and a do-not-retry instruction; ours blocks in a FIFO queue and eventually succeeds, so the model never learns it over-fanned-out. (4) MISSING CONTROLS — no `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` equivalent (the repo's mapping convention would make it `NESSY_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, cf. `NESSY_FORK_SUBAGENT` at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:54-56), no ultracode exemption, and no `/subtask` exemption (:908) — ours can block a user-started fork behind a background fan-out. Resume is already effectively unchecked, so :909 needs no change. Secondary: the doc's limit is per SESSION; ours is per Pi subprocess, and `SessionManager.ts:11143` min-clamps a nested child's inherited `concurrency`, so a deep tree's total running count is not bounded by any single counter.

DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY` sends 16 as the host-side ceiling, and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:149 hard-throws `child-session-concurrency-limit` at that number. Raising the subagent path to 20 without changing this makes that host error reachable at 16 running children. change.what: Pass `limitScope: 'workflow'` in `baseArgs` so workflow agents keep the 16 / `cpuCores - 2` semaphore and are not counted against or blocked by the subagent ceiling (:911).
Pass `limitScope: 'fork'` so the fork takes a slot but is never refused or queued (:908). One field; the admission race at :137-142 then cannot stall behind a saturated fan-out.
Pass `limitScope: 'internal'` — the review judge is a host-run child, not an Agent-tool spawn, so it must not consume the model's subagent budget.

Pass `limitScope: 'internal'` in the args forwarded to `spawn` for the same reason. The adapter forwards the args object verbatim, so add the field where the core's args are widened to `SpawnChildSessionArgs`.

Pass `limitScope: 'agent-tool'` explicitly (same as the default) so the gated path is self-documenting. Leave the resume branch at :474 alone — it already bypasses the gate, which is :909. Do not confuse this with `DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS = 100` at :23/:150: that is a per-call task-array cap, a different limit.

Two positive/negative pairs: (a) the 21st concurrent `'agent-tool'` spawn returns a `failure` whose error contains `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and succeeds again after one completes; (b) with `NESSY_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=2` the third fails, and with `thinkingLevel: () => 'max'` it does not. Also assert a `'fork'` spawn is admitted while 20 agent-tool children run, and that `'workflow'` spawns still clamp to `computeEffectiveConcurrency` (keep the existing case at :481-507 green).

Change 'Applies to' from '`subagent`, `workflow`' to '`workflow`' and add a row for the subagent ceiling (default 20, env `NESSY_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, hard failure, ultracode-exempt, fork-exempt), citing sub-agents.md:904 and :908-911.

blastRadius: Crosses a wire AND a persistence boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. `budgets.concurrency` is a field of `PiChildStartInput` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:10), is min-clamped against the inherited budget at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11143 (and pinned to 1 for plugin-hook children at :4934, :11218), is enforced at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:149, and is COPIED INTO THE PERSISTED child record at child-session-service.ts:131 — old records keep 16 after the change, so the new ceiling must not depend on a stored budget being >= it. Also validated as one of five numeric budgets at child-session-service.ts:574. In-subprocess readers of the semaphore: subagent-tool.ts:282/:316, workflow-tool.ts:358/:390, review-tool.ts:309, guardian-runner.ts:57, subtask.ts:95. Config surface: `PiOrchestratorConfig.concurrency` (harness-manifest.ts:30, default :103, validated :250, normalized :233-262), carried in `orchestratorFields` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:311) and re-read at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:233 and :1278. Keeping the new limit as a subprocess-side env read avoids touching `PiOrchestratorConfig` and therefore avoids any execution-manifest / model-contract hash change — adding a manifest field instead would put it on the hashed object and is the more expensive route. Tests that must stay green: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.test.ts:481-507 (`computeEffectiveConcurrency` table) and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:172, :370 (`child-session-concurrency-limit`). Remaining resource backstop once the Agent-tool path leaves the CPU-narrowed semaphore: the host-wide `live-agent-ceiling.ts` bound `max(2, RAM/2GiB)` with LRU eviction — worth a deliberate check on a 4-core / 8 GiB machine, since 20 concurrent Pi children is a heavier fan-out than we have ever allowed.
userImpact: Observable, on the fan-out that Nessy advertises. The effective subagent cap is `min(16, cores - 2)`: 6 on a typical 8-core laptop, 2 on a 4-core one. A `subagent` parallel call with 12 tasks starts 6 and silently queues the other 6 — no error, no badge, no reason shown — so a wave Claude Code would run at once takes two or three, and the model, never seeing a refusal, keeps requesting fan-outs the machine will serialize. There is no user or admin knob to raise it. Worse and sharper: `/subtask` blocks. `startSubtaskFork` awaits admission (subtask.ts:137-142) through the same semaphore, so while a background fan-out holds every slot, the user's `/subtask` produces no fork panel and no error until a slot frees — the doc's exact promise is that this fork is 'never blocked by the limit'. Nothing in the product ever prints `Concurrent subagent limit reached`.
